headline: 3 core bridge contracts catalogued on Ethereum: L1 Standard Bridge proxy/implementation, Cross-Domain Messenger

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search for 'Mantle Bridge' on Ethereum identified L1 Standard Bridge Proxy at 0x95fC37A27a2f68e3A647CDc081F0A89bb47c3012 with verified source code and proxy pattern.
Official bridge at https://app.mantle.xyz/bridge references bridge token mapping in Mantle documentation; no explicit deployed-contracts-doc found on main website.

OpenZeppelin audit report (blog.openzeppelin.com) for Mantle Token and Bridge identified in-scope bridge contracts and confirmed L1StandardBridge is a fork of Optimism bridge with MNT-specific handling.
No GitHub repository pinned in per-protocol context; deployment artifacts cannot be verified from source control.
Only Ethereum chain pinned in protocol.chains; single-chain deployment reduces enumeration scope.
L1 Standard Bridge is not a factory pattern; no child contract enumeration required.
Identified role taxonomy: proxy_admin (creator address), messenger (cross-domain mediator), and bridge implementation contract. Ownership inferred from contract creator and constructor arguments.
All discovered addresses traced to Etherscan direct fetches; token address also cited in official Mantle documentation onboarding guide.

rationale.verdict: Discovery phase enumerated three core on-chain contracts on Ethereum mainnet: L1 Standard Bridge (proxy at 0x95fC37A27a2f68e3A647CDc081F0A89bb47c3012, implementation at 0xb4133552BA49dFb60DA6eb5cA0102d0f94ce071f), and MNT token (0x3c3a81e81dc49a522a592e7622a7e711c06bf354). Cross-domain messenger identified from constructor args. No GitHub source was provided to discover additional deployment artifacts. Bridge token mappings referenced in official documentation but not enumerated here.

evidence.shows: L1 Standard Bridge Proxy with verified source code; constructor sets owner to 0x2A2954F3989a83Cc43DD58B0f038D5F276f21333; implementation points to 0xb4133552ba49dfb60da6eb5ca0102d0f94ce071f
L1StandardBridge implementation contract with verified source; constructor args reveal _messenger=0x676A795fe6E43C17c668de16730c3F690FEB7120 and _l1mnt=0x3c3a81e81dc49a522a592e7622a7e711c06bf354
OpenZeppelin audit report describing L1StandardBridge as fork of Optimism bridge with MNT-specific logic; dated August 26, 2025; confirms bridge handles ETH, ERC-20, and MNT token types
Official Mantle documentation onboarding guide lists MNT token address as 0x3c3a81e81dc49A522A592e7622A7E711c06bf354 on Ethereum Mainnet; cites Etherscan link for official contract

unknowns: D2: No canonical 'Deployed Contracts' documentation page found on protocol.website or docs.mantle.xyz; bridge token mapping referenced but URL not fetched
D4: No GitHub repository recorded in per-protocol context; cannot verify deployment artifacts or canonical commit SHAs
D6: Factory-pattern child contracts not enumerated; unknown whether bridge maintains dynamic token pair registry beyond hard-coded MNT
D8: Creator address 0x2A2954F3989a83Cc43DD58B0f038D5F276f21333 not yet read on-chain to determine if EOA or multisig

protocol_metadata.about: Mantle Bridge is an L1-L2 canonical bridge enabling asset transfers between Ethereum Mainnet (L1) and Mantle Network (L2). It is a fork of the Optimism Standard Bridge extended to handle the native MNT gas token alongside standard ERC-20 tokens and ETH. The bridge implements optimistic rollup mechanics with a challenge period for withdrawals.
